screening.reason: Inclusion 2/3: analyses ABIDE resting-state BOLD fMRI explicitly and reports a group-difference analysis between ASD and typical control subjects.

evidence_spans.text: Anatomical and functional data from fifty-five subjects with ASD (12.7 ± 2.4 y/o) and 55 age- matched (14.1 ± 3.1 y/o) healthy controls were accessed through the NITRC database and the ABIDE project.
evidence_spans.claim: Cohort: 55 ASD and 55 age-matched typical control subjects from ABIDE.

evidence_spans.text: Diagnosis was established with the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) [39], the Autism Diagnostic Interview Revised (ADI-R) [40] as well as clini- cal consensus.
evidence_spans.claim: Diagnosis established via ADOS, ADI-R and clinical consensus.

evidence_spans.text: The 240 regions of interest (ROIs) defined for this study were extracted from the TT_Daemon human brain atlas [43] provided with the AFNI package [44].
evidence_spans.claim: ROI analysis used the TT_Daemon atlas via AFNI.

evidence_spans.text: The rs-BOLD data were corrected for motion artifacts using a time series general affine registration for 12 parameters (3dWarpDrive/AFNI).
evidence_spans.claim: Motion correction performed via AFNI 3dWarpDrive 12-parameter affine registration.

evidence_spans.text: We found that the main regions, where signal complexity significantly decreased among ASD patients, were the amygdala (p = 0.001), the vermis (p = 0.02), the basal ganglia (p = 0.01) and the hippocampus (p = 0.02).
evidence_spans.claim: ASD patients showed significantly decreased fractal-dimension signal complexity in the amygdala, vermis, basal ganglia and hippocampus.

evidence_spans.text: This indicates that there were no regions where signal complexity signifi- cantly increased respect to controls among the ASD patients.
evidence_spans.claim: No brain regions showed significantly increased signal complexity in ASD relative to controls; changes were unidirectional (decreased).

evidence_spans.text: Overall, we found reduced signal complexity in the ASD subjects with respect to controls.
evidence_spans.claim: Overall summary finding: reduced rs-BOLD signal complexity (fractal dimension) in ASD vs. controls.

evidence_spans.text: We downloaded data from the publicly accessible ABIDE-1 database: http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/ abide_I
evidence_spans.claim: Data sourced from the publicly accessible ABIDE I database.

assessments.support: 55 ASD and 55 age-matched controls, with demographic table (age, IQ, sex ratio, handedness, ADI-R/ADOS scores).
Table 1 reports age, IQ, sex/handedness ratios and ADI-R/ADOS scores for both groups; acquisition described (3T GE Signa, 32-channel coil).
AFNI-based motion correction, N27-atlas spatial warping, and TT_Daemon ROI atlas explicitly described, plus a custom fractal-dimension (Hurst exponent) analysis pipeline detailed step by step.
Diagnosis established via ADOS, ADI-R and clinical consensus, explicitly stated.

Groups are age-matched, but sex ratio differs markedly between groups (46:9 ASD vs 38:17 controls) and is not statistically addressed; site is not discussed (appears to be a single-scanner/site subset) and motion is not quantified with a standard FD metric.
No explicit covariate adjustment for sex imbalance or head motion is reported; authors note most ASD patients were on psychotropic medication and chose not to exclude them.
Fractal dimension (Hurst exponent via power spectral density and dispersional analysis) computed voxelwise and validated against normality tests.
Z-score thresholding (|Z|>2.0) and region-wise p-values are reported, but no explicit multiple-comparisons correction (e.g. FDR/Bonferroni) across the 240 ROIs is described.

risk_of_bias.summary: A methodologically detailed single-cohort ABIDE associational study (custom fractal-dimension analysis) with clear diagnostic criteria and pipeline description, but unclear handling of sex imbalance, site, head-motion quantification, and multiple-comparisons correction.

charting.title: Temporal fractal analysis of the rs-BOLD signal identifies brain abnormalities in autism spectrum disorder
charting.authors: Dona O; Hall GB; Noseworthy MD
charting.medications_therapies: Most ASD patients received psychotropic medication; not excluded
charting.severity_levels: ADI-R total (mean 41.6, SD 8.7), ADOS severity (mean 6.5, SD 2.2)
charting.dataset_openly_available: Data sourced from the publicly accessible ABIDE I database
charting.specific_features: Voxelwise fractal dimension (FD = 2-H) of the rs-BOLD signal over 240 TT_Daemon ROIs
charting.feature_extraction_tools: Custom AFNI-based pipeline (3dWarpDrive motion correction, N27 atlas warping)
charting.feature_change_direction: Decreased fractal dimension (signal complexity) in ASD vs. controls; no regions showed significantly increased complexity
charting.summary_key_findings: A custom fractal-dimension (Hurst exponent) analysis of rs-BOLD signal complexity in 55 ASD and 55 age-matched controls from ABIDE found significantly decreased signal complexity in ASD in the amygdala (p=0.001), vermis (p=0.02), basal ganglia (p=0.01) and hippocampus (p=0.02), with no regions showing significantly increased complexity in ASD; fractal dimension in several ROIs correlated with ADI-R/ADOS severity scores.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Amygdala, vermis, basal ganglia, hippocampus (decreased signal complexity in ASD)

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Group-difference (associational); ABIDE I; 55 ASD and 55 age-matched typical controls (apparently single-scanner/site cohort, 3T GE Signa)
narrative_row.methods: Custom AFNI-based pipeline (3dWarpDrive motion correction, N27 atlas warping); voxelwise fractal dimension (Hurst exponent) computed over 240 TT_Daemon ROIs; Z-score thresholding and Pearson correlation with ADI-R/ADOS severity scores
narrative_row.outcomes: Significantly decreased signal complexity (fractal dimension) in ASD in the amygdala (p=0.001), vermis (p=0.02), basal ganglia (p=0.01) and hippocampus (p=0.02); no regions showed significantly increased complexity in ASD; FD in several ROIs correlated with ADI-R/ADOS scores
narrative_row.key_limitations: Sex ratio differs between groups without reported adjustment; no standard motion-exclusion threshold or explicit multiple-comparisons correction reported; most ASD patients were medicated and not excluded
narrative_row.relevance_notes: A non-standard (fractal-dimension) connectivity analysis method applied to an ABIDE subset, useful for linking methodological diversity within the dataset-publication knowledge graph

kg_link.cohort_description: 55 ASD and 55 age-matched typically developing controls accessed via NITRC/ABIDE, apparently from a single acquisition site/scanner (3T GE Signa, 32-channel coil)
kg_link.pipeline: Custom AFNI-based pipeline (3dWarpDrive motion correction, N27 atlas warping)
kg_link.finding: ASD patients show significantly decreased rs-BOLD fractal-dimension signal complexity relative to controls in the amygdala (p=0.001), vermis (p=0.02), basal ganglia (p=0.01) and hippocampus (p=0.02), with no regions showing significantly increased complexity.
evidence_quotes: Anatomical and functional data from fifty-five subjects with ASD (12.7 ± 2.4 y/o) and 55 age- matched (14.1 ± 3.1 y/o) healthy controls were accessed through the NITRC database and the ABIDE project.

We found that the main regions, where signal complexity significantly decreased among ASD patients, were the amygdala (p = 0.001), the vermis (p = 0.02), the basal ganglia (p = 0.01) and the hippocampus (p = 0.02).
